versions.short: The bill would let the Secretary of the Interior enter into a one-time agreement, lasting up to five years, with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation, a nonprofit partner of Gateway Arch National Park, so the foundation could host private events at the park, including in certain park buildings such as the Arch Visitor Center and the Old Courthouse. The agreement would have to set protections for the park, including limits on event dates and times, a monthly cap on events, staffing levels for safety and resource protection, liability insurance naming the United States, and a release of federal liability for injuries. Events would have to fit the park's purposes, could not degrade the park or block public access, and the Secretary would charge fees to cover wear and tear and could recover the full costs of the events. The bill would also keep the National Park Service free to host its own events and issue other permits, end the foundation authority and any existing agreement seven years after enactment, and require a report to Congress within four years evaluating the agreement's operational and financial effects.
